message.content:
I see. The `REFILL_BITS_BRANCHLESS()` macro reads a full machine word (`get_unaligned_leword(in_next)`) from the input buffer. This is the overread. When `in_end - in_next >= sizeof(bitbuf_t)`, it reads a full word. But the issue is that this reads up to `sizeof(bitbuf_t)` bytes, and if the input buffer ends right at the boundary of a heap allocation, this read can go past the end of the buffer.

Actually, the key insight from the vulnerability description: "a 16-bit unaligned read (get_unaligned_be16/load_u16_unaligned) can read two bytes past the end of the input buffer". This is in the zlib header parsing at line 49: `hdr = get_unaligned_be16(in_next);`. 

Wait, but there's a check `if (in_nbytes < ZLIB_MIN_OVERHEAD) return LIBDEFLATE_BAD_DATA;`. Let me check ZLIB_MIN_HEADER_SIZE.
